marker: # unit_length is the repeat unit length printed for each marker in Table 3, which agrees with the
# Repeat units column of Table 2 for every locus except bams13: Table 2 gives 39 bp there, while
# Table 3, the sequenced allele sizes and the reference assembly all give 9 bp, so 39 appears to
# ref_size is the product measured in the Ames Ancestor assembly GCA_000008445.1 by in silico PCR
# with these primers. Every one of the 25 sizes falls inside the fragment size range Table 2 gives
# for that locus, and 24 of them are also a row of Table 3; vrrC1 is the exception and is covered
# by the correction the Methods applies to that locus, 583 bp read as 580 bp.
# ref_repeats is the repeat number Table 3 pairs with that size. For the eight MLVA-8 loci the
# Methods states the same values in full: the Ames code 314-229-153-580-532-158-126-141 bp is
# 10-16-6-53-17-2-7-10 repeats for vrrA, vrrB1, vrrB2, vrrC1, vrrC2, CG3, pXO1-aat and pXO2-at.
# THIS NUMBERING IS NOT THE ONE USED BY bacillus_mlva31_mlvabank OR bacillus_mlva8_keim_2000.
# Those schemes take their copy numbers from the MLVAbank locus identifiers, which count the same
# reference products differently at five loci: vrrA 4 against 10 here, vrrB1 20 against 16,
# vrrB2 13 against 6, pXO2-at 9 against 10 and bams34 11 against 9. The sizes agree exactly at
# every locus. A profile from this scheme is comparable with published MLVA-25 genotypes and a
# profile from those schemes is not, and the two must not be mixed.
# patterns are kept only for the two loci whose published repeat number equals the number of times
# the motif occurs in the reference, so the tandem array cross-check is active there and skipped
# elsewhere, where it would contradict the published number. vrrA carries no pattern here although
# bacillus_mlva31_mlvabank gives it one, because the counter finds the four perfect 12 bp copies
# that panel numbers rather than the ten this one does.
